The posts defend it in their own words. @eff.org writes, “Corporations made trillions of dollars off of a foundation of open-source software like PHP; the vulnerability apocalypse could destroy that foundation. perspectives.title: War Dogs
perspectives.summary: Genetic engineering of war dogs is unnecessary and cruel

representative_posts.author: nvbinder.io
representative_posts.text: we already genetically engineered perfect war dogs

representative_posts.author: therascalking.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: And also, just a stupid point, don't they already have fucking fully armed robot dogs now? Why do they need to spend fortunes on some weird genetic experiments on dogs, intended to fight wars from 100 years ago. What sort of wars are they imagining coming, where we'd be using fucking dogs?

representative_posts.author: adaloveslace.eurosky.social
representative_posts.text: They couldn't think of a better cause to put their billions of dollars toward, so... genetically enhanced war dogs!

representative_posts.author: aaronboyde1776.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Warhound: Genetic engineering is coming to America's war dogs

representative_posts.author: randymiller.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: dogs already serve roles in the military though, I don't think even these guys are deluded enough to think they can breed a dog soldier that can operate independently of a human canine handler

representative_posts.author: courtneymilan.com
representative_posts.text: The actual thing “war dogs” need is regular dogs, but mistreated so that they lash out in anger. That’s the thing you would do to make war dogs: massive animal cruelty that, by the way, would be very difficult to target.

representative_posts.author: warrenterra.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It's so fucking bizarre. To the extent there could be uses for dogs in the military - and I'm leaving aside ethics entirely here, because the hypothetical person wanting this definitely sucks - there would be absolutely zero need to edit the dogs' genomes, and no justification for the insane cost.

representative_posts.author: dfluke.net
representative_posts.text: (re. PR about possible genetically modified murder dogs) reminder of how trained US Military personnel on active duty, "their boys", cornfed Americans, whomst they doth tanketh for their vile service for a mass murderous, fascist hegemony, treat dogs

representative_posts.author: zoognosisjoy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It is abuse. We need to abolish police dogs and war dogs, full stop. Even worse that they're using CRISPR gene editing to make hybrid dogs with unknown future health risks.

representative_posts.author: ernekid.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This is a stupid fucking idea for a bunch of reasons but namely it’s hard to improve on the dogs we already use for the military. You’re not getting any better than a German Shepherd.

representative_posts.author: grittybeard.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Aside from all the terrifying sounding stuff we're reinventing something again that is already here? We've spent thousands of years creating dogs that are good at things, and if your thing is breeding a dog that is good for troops to use that's already a thing we have.

representative_posts.author: yourcanadiangf.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: how many dogs are they going to slaughter in their "genetic" experiments? and why breed "war dogs" when there are already robotic dogs with flamethrowers happening?

representative_posts.author: iramjohn.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Apart from all the ethical concerns, there's the issue of whether we understand the relationships between genetics and behaviour in dogs well enough to achieve something like this. You want to genetically engineer war Drosophila? I'd guess the knowledge is there. War rats? Doubtful, but maybe.

representative_posts.author: kincheloe.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: why the fkk do we need war dogs????!!!

representative_posts.author: zoognosisjoy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I wager that this venture capital firm is going to introduce a few key gene edits to a GSD and call it a day. There are other dogs initially bred for violence (Mastiffs, bulldogs), but GSDs are specifically the dog of modern militarism.

representative_posts.author: mrpaulymac.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: These dipshits really think hyperintelligent attack dogs don't exist and think this is an untapped market. 1.2 billion dollar valuation for what's essentially a puppy mill

representative_posts.author: monsterteatime.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The "war dogs" thing is just the Rat-things but like...much dumber.

representative_posts.author: shazamablama.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: No one wants war dogs. Come on! For fuck sake humans just stop being idiots.

representative_posts.author: anitmata.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think they could make dogs both a) more dangerous to humans and b) very trainable IDK why they need $1.2B to *engineer* them, though, when selective breeding is *right there*

representative_posts.author: pappyparki.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A contractor famous for not producing military equipment that actually works on the battlefield being funded by Don Jr & getting sweetheart contracts from Trump is working on genetically altered war dogs. Besides abhorrent & cruel, this doesn't end well for dogs or man

representative_posts.author: neveltenjohn.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: What is wrong with this? Military dogs are mostly used for recon, but even if they were primarily attack dogs, do you oppose all new weapon R&D?

representative_posts.author: ultralaser.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: this is either a - fraud, just fraud, they will spend 50mill of 1.2bn on "dog research" and pocket the rest b - incredibly misguided 'genetic' research based on long discredited alpha behavioral science to make like a super asshole dog c - animal abuse d - feeding dogs to the army one at at time

representative_posts.author: sarenraesaves.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Worst case: some unholy cross of every giant livestock guardian breed + wolf dogs + selection for "warrior spirit" creates 200-lb paranoiacs who refuse to work w/anyone they haven't known from a puppy. A wash as military dogs, find a niche w/Finnish moose hunters.

representative_posts.author: lostinapapercup.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think the point above (this isn't for military combat, it's to kill/maim/deter protestors) is probably correct. However, even fancy designer dogs are also probably much cheaper than munitions (which we are apparently running out of), especially as they are a renewable resource.

representative_posts.author: opensecretalien.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: How else are they supposed to create a whole new breed of dogs? By letting them screw?

genetic engineering is not needed for war dogs
creating war dogs is cruel and abusive

perspectives.title: First Cinema Visit
perspectives.summary: People recall their first cinema visit

representative_posts.author: tomewing.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Genuinely can’t remember, sorry cinephiles. I know where it would have been - Saturday matinee at the Thorndike Theatre Leatherhead which doubled as a cinema for the kids, probably in 78 or 79. But whatever it was it instilled in me a lifelong broad apathy about the movies!

representative_posts.author: dasmunch.eurosky.social
representative_posts.text: Disney's Robin Hood at the Sheppey Cinema. I must have been five. I remember being hugely jealous later that year because my friend James went to the Cannon cinema in Sittingbourne to see Back To The Future

representative_posts.author: janehill.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Other than Saturday morning cinema, the first one I really remember is Snowball Express, 1972, at the Odeon on the corner of Festing Road in Southsea. Lovely cinema, still feel angry whenever I revisit my old haunts that it’s no longer there.

representative_posts.author: centuriesofsound.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I was definitely taken to the cinema as a small child, most likely to see Disney classics, but do I remember any? No, I do not.

representative_posts.author: twofatfeet.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If you ignore the Saturday morning kids’ programmes, the first time I remember going to the cinema would have either been a cartoon version of Alice in Wonderland or Candleshoe. At least one of those would have been in 1977 because there were posters for Star Wars and I wanted to see that instead

representative_posts.author: starstormx1.eurosky.social
representative_posts.text: ...dangit, I was taken to my first movie theater WAY too young to remember anything! Well, aside from the Cineplex Odeon presentation package at the time. Had some vague memories of them that got reignited watching uploads and realizing "oh yeah, I think I saw this"

representative_posts.author: zedekyr.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Digger (2026) was phenomenal. A few movies really stick with me but I don't think I'll have a theatre experience like that again, at least as authentically as the first time watching.

representative_posts.author: merseytart.com
representative_posts.text: Snow White, 1980, cinema in Bury Park, Luton. I was three and my mum worried I’d fidget and get bored. Instead I sat absolutely rapt and didn’t move an inch. It was, after all, a big telly.

representative_posts.author: bringthenoise.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: First NEW film I remember was Suburban Commando at the same cinema in 1991. A rare cinema outing for my Dad, we were sent out to clear the house for my Mum to run a Tupperware party. I think I enjoyed the big promotional cup with straw I was bought more than the movie.

representative_posts.author: bexxi.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: First film you saw at the cinema. The real first one, not the pretend one you tell people! Film, year, where, & whatever stuck with you. The Slipper & the Rose. Commodore, Aberystwyth, 1976. I remember NOTHING except that Dad took me; it might be the only time we ever went to the cinema together.

representative_posts.author: careyart.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Sleeping Beauty, 1972, probably the Odeon Cinema Brighton. I'd have been around 4 and the only memory I have is also one of my earliest memories, which is being absolutely terrified of Maleficient as the dragon at the end. Gave me nightmares for years after

representative_posts.author: richard0x4a.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think it was The Dark Crystal, at Ripon Cinema, probably in 1982 when I was 7. I can remember my Grandma getting so thoroughly involved in the film that she called out "Fly!" at some key moment in the middle of the cinema. Great film.

representative_posts.author: hughsykes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The Hound of the Baskervilles (I t h i n k). Palace Cinema, Devizes. 1960 ish. I was nine. I remember enjoying the blend of fear & suspense, & thinking Dartmoor looked excitingly spooky. (My memory of it is monochrome, but it says here it was colour). My 6-year-old brother David had nightmares.

representative_posts.author: thewrittentevs.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It would've been "Barney's Great Adventure". I was taken to see it by my parents at the now-demolished Showcase Cinema in Walsall. (Bless their ability to sit through stuff that they must've thought was complete bullshit.)

representative_posts.author: housedokpro.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: First film you saw at the cinema: Thanks to a lack of babysitting: Reds (1981) There may have been others before this, but apparently I talked through this film. Although I don't remember anything about it.

representative_posts.author: putnam39.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Masters of the Universe, 1987, my dad and I were the only ones in the theater The first one I saw without a parent (or adult), Edward Scissorhands, 1991, with my friend Patrick at a 2-screen theater called the Da-Bel. It was eventually closed and razed for a Rite-Aid pharmacy

representative_posts.author: cinemaseconds.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I had tired to see in the cinema but alas, it was here I think at the BIFFF once if I remember correct, but I was out of the country that week ( who know if I remember this correctly it was ages ago) either way a good film.

representative_posts.author: smudgeboy99.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The Love Bug - came out in 1968 but Mum took me to see it in the summer holidays of 1970, when I was aged 6, at the now long-gone Odeon Cinema in South Norwood.

representative_posts.author: jimmywim.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The Secret Garden 1993. I was 8 years old and I could have sworn I went to the cinema to see the first Turtles movie in 1990, but got no real memory of it. I remember being taken away by Secret Garden though, and it embedded an appreciation of stately home gardens ever since. And very old doors.

representative_posts.author: joshmlee.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: First film you saw at the cinema. The real first one, not the pretend one you tell people! Didn’t like it as much as a kid, I like it a lot more now as an adult. I’ve been told I saw Lion King in a Drive-In, but I genuinely do not remember that experience.

representative_posts.author: laikax.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: farmersboy.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: mthrjo.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Snow White, which was rereleased in 1987 for its fifty year anniversary. It was a cinema in Edinburgh, but I don’t remember which one - possibly the Dominion in Morningside? I remember being very scared of the Queen, the the dwarves singing, and also Snow White and the birds.

representative_posts.author: keithnokes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The first I remember in a theater was actually Star Wars, somewhere near Hartford CT, for my friend's 6th birthday. I remember his mom somehow was allowed to bring big bags of home-popped popcorn to share. Pretty sure I saw one of those Herbie movies at a drive-in sometime before that though.

representative_posts.author: dubdobdee.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: p sure it was THE INCREDIBLE JOURNEY (1963) tho probably not *in* 1963 as i was too small to be in a cinema that year

representative_posts.author: rootsbelow.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: discokidnap.northsky.social

representative_posts.author: badgerbadgerbadger.ca

representative_posts.author: mjowen174.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: lesbiankrile.etheirys.social

representative_posts.author: partyinthefront.bsky.social

representative_posts.text: In between meetings and writing and admin stuff, I changed the bedding, washed/folded the bed linens, vacuumed the bedroom carpets, and cleaned the toilets. Tomorrow, I'll be able to sleep in and rest.

representative_posts.author: lordoflezzies.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: There should be an option in my sleep settings to say "I have cats" to explain why I wake up almost 10 times in the 2 hours before my alarm goes off, because "is it breakfast time yet?"

representative_posts.author: takasugivapes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 5 hours of uninterrupted sleep last night. i am a human weapon

representative_posts.author: chickorycat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Before you go to sleep, choose one moment from the day you want to keep. When your days are filled with stress & anxiety, the good moments can get lost in the chaos. We can forget what makes life worth living. At the end of the day, there is always something good. Let's rewire our brains to find it.

representative_posts.author: smolizzyhands.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: logorrhea to be fair, that's absolutely who i am an insomniac who can't shut up i went to urgent care today for another toradol shot, that might be part of why i'm so verbose tonight shit hurts but not as much as it did last night i'm getting sleepy, though it's cold and rainy rn

representative_posts.author: barelyashley.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Me sleeping all day and waking up to all of my notifications across platforms.

representative_posts.author: rojohen.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Once every two months or so, I get one really good, quality night’s sleep, and I wake up early, feeling rested, and ready to conquer the world. Today is that day.

representative_posts.author: dezlet.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Three days of little to no sleep but! At least I slept five hours in a row last night So I should be fine to work tonight

representative_posts.author: sinisterporpoise.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I will never get used to it being so dark so late in the morning here, even if I like that it stays sunnier later because it better fits my overall sleep cycle. Maybe one day I will return home and see what I am used to again.

representative_posts.author: rivercavy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yep can’t motivate myself out the bed. More sleep it is.

representative_posts.author: dancequeenem.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Idk what is up with my child but this is day 5 of her waking up between 3:30 & 5AM (typically she sleeps until 8:30 or later) and having major tantrums/meltdowns. Then because she’s up so early she’s falling asleep anywhere from 2-5 hours earlier at night which is not helping the issue at all.

I find myself losing sleep on Tuesday nights
I'm so tired but can't sleep
I need a blessing from the sleep gods

Health.name: Smoking Bans

perspectives.title: Smoking Bans
perspectives.summary: Smoking is no longer allowed in public spaces

representative_posts.author: mahelious.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I do not miss the smoking sections of restaurants or hotels. If you were in the first booth of the "non-smoking" section it was guaranteed that food would taste like cigarette ash.

representative_posts.author: dixonij.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The utter obliteration of smoking sections in restaurants when people started taking secondhand smoke damage seriously in the early 2000's

representative_posts.author: holyshitimfucked.com
representative_posts.text: It happened on a generational divide. Young smokers just started going outside to smoke. Don't know if it was carryover from smoking being disallowed in restaurants and workplaces.

representative_posts.author: sergalprojects.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: On that note, everyone ever notice how much *better* everything smells in public spaces after the smoking bans?

representative_posts.author: ppu512.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Im old enough to remember going to restaurants with smoking sections, and my dad was a smoker, and my clothes would stink like a tobacco and tar bonfire by the end of every visit with him. Vaping, at least, doesn't get into your hair and clothes like that.

representative_posts.author: woozle2023.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Smoking eliminated in restaurants and other public spaces. Seat belt requirements and car seats for babies & children.

representative_posts.author: awfullyvague.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: (Lack of) smoking. We made ashtrays for our parents in art class and no one thought this was the tiniest bit strange. In California you can only smoke in designated areas and most of those are in Nevada. It's great.

representative_posts.author: doronjosama.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I misread this at first as a Beavis & Butthead style "Smoking rules!" statement, but figured it out pretty quick. 😅 And yes, everyone smoked everywhere in public with scant regard for who was around. Many of my elementary school friends had scars from walking into a lit cigarette held at kid-level.

representative_posts.author: kayorchison.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: There was a smoking section on a 747 I was on as a kid. There was a smoking section on a fkn COACH with sealed windows. "Section" You know a plane has been around for a while when you find ashtrays in the armrests.

representative_posts.author: billashumet.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The reduction of cigarette smoking, taking on big tobacco was a huge effort. In the 70’s flying back from Europe on leave everyone on the plane it seemed lit up a cigarette, 6 hour flight in a cloud of smoke.

representative_posts.author: emmalufc.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yeah as a family we used to sit in the smoking section so my dad could have a cigar. He wouldn't dream of doing the same to my kids. Times have changed for the better

representative_posts.author: stephenjwild.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: In my early 20s I worked in a bar that still permitted smoking. It was gross (but paid well). We have come far (laudatory).

representative_posts.author: civ5fan.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Not having smoking in restaurants.

representative_posts.author: dbvirago.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This. People today could never imagine sitting in a restaurant next to a guy that puts his cigarette out in his mashed potatoes. Or sitting in a 'no smoking row' on an airplane where 50 people have lit up. Or having your doctor come into the exam room smoking.

representative_posts.author: brianbo.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Uh, what type of smoking?

representative_posts.author: justbru.ce.it
representative_posts.text: Non-smoking most stuff! Makes me really appreciate how bad stuff used to be in a smoking world raised by smoking parents.

representative_posts.author: ahumblebard.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Everything, and I mean EVERYTHING, used to smell and taste like cigarette smoke and ash. We had smoking sections in family restaurants and ashtrays on planes. Even if you didn't smoke you smelled like you did. The world no longer smells of ashtray, and that's nice.

representative_posts.author: fact-or-opinion.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: As a former smoker, this a good one. Maybe the reason I started was because it felt like nearly every adult in my life was a smoker so early access was easy and inevitable. Smoking bans gave me the perspective to know I was a smelly mess and the ever increasing taxes eventually made it untenable.

representative_posts.author: courier429.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Preferably from a place that looks like people should be smoking cigarettes indoors.

representative_posts.author: petrachor.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yep. I recall teachers smoking in the teacher's lounge too.

representative_posts.author: ladyrheanon.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: No smoking indoors. Seriously. Adults in my life fought that one tooth and nail when I was a kid, but the fact of the matter is that indoor smoking bans improved the quality of life for everyone.

representative_posts.author: truebluemajority.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Elevators. People used to smoke in elevators. Hospitals! People used to smoke in HOSPITALS! Some areas were designated as no smoking for specific reasons, but there were lots of places in hospitals where smoking was allowed.

representative_posts.author: adownie.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Oh god, yes! And no more smoking on planes!

representative_posts.author: lyndonmarquis.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Pretty happy with the smoking ban in the UK…

representative_posts.author: ppushbike.eurosky.social
representative_posts.text: THE SMOKING BAN Going for a night out, or even just to the pub, and not having to: - take my asthma inhaler with me - dose up with antihistamines - throw all clothes straight in the wash when returning home - shower before going to bed to reduce the effect on my eczema

representative_posts.author: mikefa.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Hard to beat “smoking” But suggest how far golfers can now hit a little white ball! Talk about smoking I can remember an episode of The Royal on TV where the surgeon told the patient his op would take at least two pipe fulls 😮 it was a big pipe too

representative_posts.author: fredamohr.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Very disgruntled that the not smoking oui’d thing seems to be a permanent need now. Says my respiratory system. Oh well. At least I can eat it sometimes

representative_posts.author: tmwillia828.blacksky.app
representative_posts.text: Girl. DM me if you have smoker ??—I had to leave my smoker (and huge roll of butcher paper for wrapping during The Stall) in TX. I can smoke vicariously through you 🤣🤗 I also like the Franklin BBQ cookbook for brisket smoking tips. And congrats on the life reset. You were missed 😉

representative_posts.author: notyournegro.blacksky.app
representative_posts.text: Over the summer I really locked in on my BBQ and smoking techniques and I’m planning to use my smoker this holiday season and maybe discover some baker/smoking technique. I don’t know if that’s a thing……but I’m gonna find out. lol

representative_posts.author: cuw.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So much fucking better, it’s not even fair to compare the shit we were smoking even 10 years ago to today

representative_posts.author: jillehughes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I hate smoking but I used to love these as a kid. They had a nice flavor. A fruity spearmint blend.

representative_posts.author: kurth91.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: the last enforcer who took things seriously died from smoking 72 cigarettes in one day so this is technically right

public spaces smell better without smoking
smoking bans improved quality of life

Health.name: Dementia Symptoms

perspectives.title: Dementia Symptoms

representative_posts.author: sdambrosio.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Dementia

representative_posts.author: dr-g.myatproto.social
representative_posts.text: His brain being cooked by dementia is likely making all that shit even worse. His filters such as they were are failing rapidly

representative_posts.author: jim85716.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You know, a sign of increasing dementia is the loss of filter (i.e. someone whose mind is filth can’t help but use filthy language).

representative_posts.author: boudica24.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Dementia is dementia'ing

representative_posts.author: sdambrosio.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Dementia senile

representative_posts.author: rnratchett.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Symptom of dementia….. just speaking from professional experience

representative_posts.author: vkonduru.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: While we lament that this “sick” creep dozes off often in public places, it’s worse to see his mouth run any words at all also. Whether he dozes off or barely exists w/ dementia, it’s a painful thing for us to watch and endure his unbounded BS generative SI.

representative_posts.author: claypotter.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Dementia makes you think your dreams are reality.

representative_posts.author: davidjohnurban.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: wow, that is a sure sign of dementia. Just like when he could not figure out why the old saying goes "clean as a baby's ass" when obviously no one ever said that. The saying he knew when his brain worked was "smooth as a baby's bottom".

representative_posts.author: 70lesprec.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I just listened to an Expert on Aging Brain disease Alzheimers And Dementia. Alzheimers the mind forgets everything and patient becomes in the end docile Comatose. Dementia patients become more and more violent and uncontrollable as disease progresses Trump exhibits advanced Dementia

representative_posts.author: carelesswhisperer.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think it won’t be long before the dementia causes him to blurt that (and many other epithets) out.

representative_posts.author: zoe10110.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We need the PhD dementia therapist guy on this lol

representative_posts.author: mombida.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You are correct. Once a moron, always a moron. His Dementia has just accentuated it!

representative_posts.author: bob-garner.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Dementia and panic are erasing his filters. Not that he had many to begin with.

representative_posts.author: bansheebanzai.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The good news: late stage of the dementia, this could spiral down real quick. Falls. More anger, more yelling. Waving at things that aren't there.

representative_posts.author: sbharvey.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I’m curious if there’s a shared brain health condition, such as dementia, between these two.

representative_posts.author: moonwink03.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: He's just going to get much worse. He's on an IV dementia regimen, but he won't stop taking Adderall and Benzos. He's taken them since he had to give up cocaine and have his septum rebuilt. He is quickly reaching the crash out paranoia phase. Dangerous for a sadistic narcissist. VOTE!

representative_posts.author: skohayes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The symptoms of frontotemporal dementia. Trump is checking off everything on the list!

representative_posts.author: too-young.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: And he has the audacity to use the r-word while pretending he’s a Christian. Oh let me not forget dementia has some of the r-word symptoms.

representative_posts.author: titlecharacter.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: His increasing dementia makes it even easier to tell that he truly has never understood the difference between aesthetics and reality.

Health.name: Covid Flu Season

perspectives.title: Vaccine Effectiveness

representative_posts.author: codechannel.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The one thing I can say for sure now that I've got covid, is without a question being extra cautious vigilant these past 6yrs, probably saved my life -- there's zero doubt without a vaccine I'd be in the hospital 😩

representative_posts.author: michael.burjack.com
representative_posts.text: Got my seasonal flu vaccine and COVID spike booster yesterday from the pharmacist at my local Co-Op. In and out in 15 minutes. No excuses not to ensure you're protected for the upcoming season. BOOK YOUR APPOINTMENT RIGHT NOW WHILE YOU'RE READING THIS. You're welcome. 💉 #covid #flu #vaccine

representative_posts.author: queermonkey.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I’m feeling like shit after getting my Covid and flu vaccines yesterday. I’m having WILD thoughts and opinions haha. Send me cock and butts and nudes and anything else to distract me from the icy breath of death that breaths upon me.

representative_posts.author: cas7217.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: People this is real! We are seeing increased admissions of patients with the Flu and it’s not good! Vaccines work!

representative_posts.author: geenance.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I've always had the vaccines. I haven't had serious illness since. And I'm not young. I will get the shots again. I do worry about getting both the flu and covid shots at the same time though. The covid vaccines were rushed and I don't think scientists understand any potential interactions.

representative_posts.author: scottnotscot.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This year's flu vaccine had an effect on me the first time in a good few years.

representative_posts.author: lorisigurdsonndp.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It’s that time of year again to get your COVID-19 and flu vaccines! Vaccines help reduce the risk of severe illness, prevent hospitalizations, and help limit the spread of these viruses. Protect yourself, protect your community, and help keep our hospitals there for the people who need them most.

representative_posts.author: mar-kg.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Strangely, vaccines agree with me. Every time, whether Covid,flu,RSV, whatever, the next day, I'm jacked.

representative_posts.author: credible-source.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: back before the covid vaccine came out and everyone was waiting anxiously, my work phished me by announcing vaccine availability

representative_posts.author: kmeekes.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: As I understand it everyone 6 months + is eligible for Flu and Covid vaccines in Ontario as of today. Please get them if you can!

perspectives.summary: Invest in renewables for energy security

representative_posts.author: djrm94.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The kind of bizarre take you come to expect from the Greens. We'll be using fossil fuels for years, even with a sprint to net-zero. You cant just turn it off. Pragmatic and realistic to use our own resources while investing the profits in sustainable and renewable energy.

representative_posts.author: skipai.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: And fossil fuels won't fix this issue. They're too ineffecient and damaging so you wouldn't get long term profits anyways. More likely to see a data centre burn down or flooded from using that sort of energy source.

representative_posts.author: lemoore.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm not disputing the relationship. I'm tired of our Govs poor decisions benefiting others at the cost of our energy security and our environment. Invest in the grid, then the renewable energy being left on the table will solve our power problem!

representative_posts.author: glostermeteor.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Heres an idea, spend some more money on renewables. It really isnt that difficult if you actually want to combat climate change.

representative_posts.author: matsps.wsocial.eu
representative_posts.text: Great to se that several of these countries leapfrog into a future based on renewables. Lower cost, no air-pollution and energy sovereignty.

representative_posts.author: ianharvey.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: No. There is an argument that using fossil fuel taxes in the short term to invest in renewables is a good idea. If we'd done that 20 years ago we'd be in great shape now. One alternative is that we just extract fossil fuels and invest nothing in renewables.

representative_posts.author: eciu.net
representative_posts.text: "It's not a race to save the polar bears anymore. It's all about industrial strategy." Renewables hitting all time records in UK & globally Gas and oil price spikes based on whims of foreign regimes highlights the case for renewables as a national security measure 693GW installed in 2025 alone

representative_posts.author: rednovaforlife.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: What that means is that money you think is wasted is because they gave too much power to the grid at a time it wasn't needed and the time gas switched in is because other renewable sources were not supplying enough. You can't flip a switch to give you more or less wind and solar.

representative_posts.author: proud-cybernat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Too effing little, too effing late. Let's just not allow them to shaft us again with our massive renewable energy.

representative_posts.author: martinitier.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If we answer more nuanced that is absolutely correct, but just as long we are too dependant to fossil fuels for transport. Cutting back on renewables is another clusterf*** by Donald O'Lantern

representative_posts.text: Alternatively, they could authorise urgent investment into residential renewables and electrification and we could both reduce the probability of needing additional pipeline capacity at the same time as improving resilience, reducing the cost of living, and make good progress on the Green Transition

Properly. The vibes are bad, everyone.”
